title: Amplification of Escherichia coli in a Continuous-Flow-PCR Microfluidic Chip and Its Detection with a Capillary Electrophoresis System
protocol: Heat the silicon wafer at 200 °C for 25 min.
Dispense 1 mL of SU-8-2075 photoresist per inch of the wafer.
Spin coat the silicon wafer using a spin coater starting from 500 rpm for 5-10 s with an acceleration of 100 rpm/s, then at 2,000 rpm for 30 s with an acceleration of 500 rpm/s.
Soft bake the silicon wafer at 65 °C for 3 min, then at 95 °C for 15 min.
Set exposure energy to 150 - 215 mJ/cm² and engrave the designed pattern using a photolithography mask.
Expose the silicon wafer with the mask.
Post-exposure bake the silicon wafer at 65 °C for 2 min, then at 95 °C for 7 min.
Immerse the silicon wafer in developer solution until microchannels are visible.
Rinse off residual developer solution with isopropanol.
Mix polydimethylsiloxane (PDMS) prepolymer and curing agent at a ratio of 10:1.
Pour mixed PDMS solution into the replica mold and solidify it at 80 °C for 60 min.
Activate slide using a plasma cleaner.
Bond PDMS microfluidic chip on activated slide.
Solidify bonded PDMS and slide at 80 °C for 30 min.
Thaw reagents completely before configuration.
Use a vortex mixer and centrifuge to ensure the reagents are well mixed.
Prepare a centrifuge tube, adding 33.75 µL of water.
Add 1.0 µL of DNA template to the centrifuge tube.
Add 0.5 µL of primer to the centrifuge tube.
Add 5.0 µL of buffer to the centrifuge tube.
Add 4.0 µL of dNTP mixture to the centrifuge tube.
Add 1.5 µL of Tween 20 to the centrifuge tube.
Add 3.5 µL of PVP to the centrifuge tube.
Finally, add 0.25 µL of DNA polymerase to the centrifuge tube.
Mix the solution by vortexing.
Prepare two positive temperature coefficient (PTC) ceramic heaters.
Prepare two solid-state relays.
Prepare two PID temperature controllers.
Attach temperature sensors to the bottom of the PTC ceramic heaters.
Connect the heater to the solid-state relay.
Connect the solid-state relay to the PID temperature controller.
Connect two solid-state relays in series and connect the power cord.
3D print a slot for the two heaters and keep the heaters on the same plane, leaving a 12 mm air gap between them.
Place the microfluidic chip on the two heaters.
Prepare a syringe pump and fix a syringe to it.
Connect a silicone tubing (0.8 mm inner diameter) with the syringe.
Connect a steel needle (0.7 mm inner diameter) to the top of the silicone tubing.
Insert the steel needle into the inlet of the microfluidic chip.
Place a pipette tip at the outlet of the chip to collect PCR products.
Use a high-voltage power supply to generate a pulsed-field electric field, noting the positive and negative electrodes.
Filter the excitation wavelength from a mercury lamp through a filter.
Place the capillary on the microscope stage.
Collect fluorescence emission with the objective.
Detect the signal using an R928 photomultiplier tube (PMT).
Observe the microscope and the capillary under dark room conditions.
Turn on the light; excitation light is collected by the objective.
Use self-developed LABVIEW software to control the power supply.
Complete data acquisition.
Set the temperature of the heaters in the CF-PCR system to 65 °C and 95 °C.
Place the microfluidic chip on the two heating blocks.
Withdraw 50 µL of PCR solution using a syringe plunger.
Fix the syringe containing the PCR solution on a syringe pump.
Insert the steel needle into the inlet of the microfluidic chip.
Set the flow rate of the pump to 10 µL/min and start the pump to push the solution through the microchannel.
Collect the PCR products at the outlet of the microfluidic chip.
Rinse the channel with ultrapure water before and after the PCR to remove impurities.
Prepare a capillary with an 8 cm total length and a 6 cm effective length.
Mix separation buffer by combining 100 µL of 1% hydroxyethylcellulose, 2 µL of 100x SYBR Green I, and 98 µL of ultrapure water to obtain 0.5% HEC with 1x SYBR Green I.
Fill the capillary with the prepared separation buffer using a vacuum pump.
Input injection voltage (800 V) and injection time (2.0 s) on the software interface.
Start the process to introduce PCR products into the capillary at 100 V/cm for 2 seconds.
Mix PCR products on the negative electrode of the electrophoresis apparatus.
Place buffer on both positive and negative electrodes.
Input a DC voltage of 800 V through the software interface.
Click the start button to initiate electrophoresis at an electric field strength of 100 V/cm.
Stop the run once all DNA fragments are separated in the capillary.
Flush the capillary with sterilized water for 1 minute after each run.
